newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks close firmer amid rate cut hopes.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks close firmer amid rate cut hopes.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed firmer on Monday, reversing huge initial losses as expectations of a rate cut on Tuesday instilled optimism, dealers said.
The general index rose 0.98 points, 0.21 percent, to 476.44 while the Ibex added 11.21 points, 0.21 percent, to 5,452.56.

Telefonica, which denied reports it was about to announce a U.S. deal with MCI, also overturned early losses to add 20 pesetas to 3,435. Dealers said a U.S. alliance may not be fully discounted, and should at least help sentiment.
Repsol nudged up 10 pesetas to 6,080 as the book-building period in this month's public share offering started.
Banesto added 5 pesetas to 1,080 after announcing a 16.8 pct rise in first quarter earnings. But the market was disappointed by negative extraordinary results, dealers said.
Dealers said expectations of a rates cut gave both bonds and the bourse strength, despite losses on Wall Street.

"Our market really doesn't want to go down. We can't ignore losses on Wall Street but it's becoming more and more clear that the story here is very different on the basis of our strong economic fundamentals" said a dealer at a Spanish bank.
